digest.component_or_area: reconciler rich-text codec cutover with state-gated echo suppression
propositions: Cloud and DC send paths must transition from plain-text to rich codecs (Markdown-aware ADF on Cloud, rendered wiki on DC) with state-based echo suppression keying on baseline value diff rather than codec round-trip law

A change-gated inline 8-byte `rich_sha` counter bounded to equality threshold RICH_REEMIT_OBSERVE_AT=2 triggers exactly one read-back GET when the same wire is pushed twice, with zero counter cost on edit-free passes and no per-pass timestamp

Emit and baseline compares use DISTINCT normalizers: emit compares `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(local))` vs `decode_inbound(remote_wire)` (both decoded, lossy round-trip cancels); baseline compares normalized LOCAL via `RichTextCodec.normalize_outbound` against `decode(baseline_wire)` to prevent false local-changed signals
Concurrent both-sides body edits retain rebar local-wins semantics (a713) and raise an outbound-field-conflict alert while storing the remote value, with no new three-way merge or LWW clock

DC WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound must be redefined as `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` to restore codec law, affecting both update and create paths (`_map_local_to_dc_fields` and `_issues._translate_create_fields`), while comment-diff dedup key remains unaffected via identity codec

Cutover is flag-gated with new config key `reconciler.rich_text_cutover` (off/cloud/dc/both, defaults off), degrades to plain-text ADF when marklas extra is absent, and is read via config at call time in apply_handlers rather than adapter-layer import to preserve core layering
